categories.main_business_segments: Shenzhen Newway Photomask Making Co., Ltd. primarily operates in the research, development, production, and sales of photomasks used in integrated circuits and display industries. Its main product lines include photomasks for flat panel displays (covering all generations G2.5 to G11 and technologies such as LCD, AMOLED, LTPS, LTPO, Mini-LED, Micro-LED, silicon-based OLED, and FMM) and semiconductor photomasks (used in IC manufacturing, packaging, semiconductor devices including discrete devices, optoelectronic devices, sensors, and MEMS). The company also provides photomasks for touch screens, PCBs, and FPCs.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company employs advanced photolithography technologies including laser direct writing for pixelated patterns, half-tone and phase shift mask (PSM) technologies, and high-precision coating and cleaning processes. It has developed proprietary manufacturing techniques for high-generation large-size photomasks, high-precision half-tone photomasks, and semiconductor photomasks down to 150nm/130nm process nodes. The production process is highly automated and customized, involving coating, exposure, development, etching, stripping, and cleaning steps under strict quality control. The company also invests in upstream technologies such as photoresist coating and defect repair to enhance product quality.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include leading domestic flat panel display manufacturers such as BOE, Tianma Microelectronics, TCL Huaxing, Shanghai Xianyao (JBD), and Huancai Star, as well as semiconductor companies including a leading domestic chip company and its suppliers, Huatian Technology, Ningbo SMIC Integration, Jingfang Semiconductor, Tongfu Microelectronics, Sanan Optoelectronics, and Guangxun Technology. The end markets served span consumer electronics (smartphones, TVs, laptops, wearables), automotive electronics, AI chips, industrial control, and emerging sectors like microdisplays and advanced semiconductor packaging.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company is headquartered in Shenzhen, China, with subsidiaries and production facilities in Chengdu and Hong Kong. Its customer base and supply chain are primarily domestic within China, but it also engages in export sales and imports key raw materials and equipment from overseas, mainly Japan, South Korea, and other countries. The company is expanding capacity in Xiamen and other Chinese regions to support domestic market growth.
categories.supply_chain_position: Shenzhen Newway Photomask operates upstream in the semiconductor and flat panel display supply chains as a critical materials supplier. It produces photomasks that serve as essential templates for lithography processes in downstream manufacturing of integrated circuits, display panels, and semiconductor packaging. The company also invests in upstream raw material technologies and collaborates with equipment suppliers, positioning itself as a key mid-to-upstream player in the photomask industry.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus is on continuous technological innovation and capacity expansion in high-generation, high-precision photomasks for both flat panel displays and semiconductors. It emphasizes breaking foreign technology monopolies, advancing semiconductor process nodes down to 28nm, and developing new photomask types such as half-tone masks, phase shift masks, and flexible display masks. R&D efforts also target advanced packaging photomasks, Micro-LED, silicon-based OLED, and coating technologies. The company invests in intelligent manufacturing, product quality improvement, and upstream material and equipment localization to enhance supply chain security and competitiveness.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through direct sales of customized photomask products to flat panel display manufacturers, semiconductor foundries, packaging companies, and other downstream customers. The company operates on a made-to-order production model with direct sales contracts and framework agreements with major clients. Revenue is recognized upon delivery and customer acceptance. The company also receives government subsidies related to technology development and production expansion.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company is a leading domestic photomask manufacturer and ranks sixth globally and second domestically in the flat panel display photomask market. It competes with international giants such as DNP, Toppan, and other Japanese and Korean firms that have historically dominated the high-generation photomask market. Shenzhen Newway Photomask has broken foreign monopolies in G11 large-size photomasks and half-tone masks, positioning itself as a key player in China’s push for domestic substitution and supply chain security.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, the company achieved operating revenue of approximately RMB 875.5 million, a 30.21% increase year-over-year, and net profit attributable to shareholders of RMB 190.86 million, up 28.27%. The company’s total assets were about RMB 2.24 billion with net assets of RMB 1.39 billion. It maintains a healthy growth trajectory driven by expanding capacity, technological upgrades, and increasing demand from downstream industries. R&D investment was RMB 37.6 million, accounting for 4.3% of revenue.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: The company offers high-precision, high-generation photomasks that are critical for the quality and yield of downstream semiconductor and display products. It differentiates itself through domestic technological leadership, breaking foreign monopolies in large-size and high-precision photomasks, and providing comprehensive product coverage across all display generations and semiconductor process nodes. Its strong customer service, fast response, and localization advantages support supply chain security and meet the increasing customization and precision demands of emerging technologies such as AMOLED, Micro-LED, advanced packaging, and third-generation semiconductors.
